title: Forecast only with information that has arrived.
discipline: Time-series ML / point-in-time data / experiment design
summary: A commodity-forecasting research system built around delayed-label availability, chronological evaluation, controlled feature studies, and recoverable execution. The strongest lesson is knowing when a promising development result does not transfer.
scope: The public commands recompute aggregate evidence and execute a synthetic delayed-label access contract. Optional browser tests exercise an online ridge demonstration using released labels only. These checks do not establish trading profitability.
private_boundary: Restricted market data, private prediction matrices, fitted research weights, current feature recipes, full orchestration, and operational cloud state remain excluded. Historical source credits and results are retained.

cards.title: Treat publication time as part of the feature contract.
cards.decision: Reject labels whose release time lies after the forecast origin instead of relying only on observation dates.
cards.boundary: The authored timing fixture is not an official data-release simulator.

cards.title: Preserve checkpoint identity across interruptions.
cards.decision: Bind persistent research state to input and configuration identities rather than assuming a file is reusable because it exists.
cards.boundary: The latest private training state is not included.

cards.title: Inspect where pooled accuracy breaks down.
cards.decision: Recompute errors by series and chronological half, retaining sample counts, bias and matched baseline errors.
cards.boundary: These are descriptive diagnostics on authored synthetic observations, with dependent target horizons.

cards.title: Compare models on the same target population.
cards.decision: Use target-composition and prediction-parity checks before interpreting an apparent metric regression.
cards.boundary: Matching a shared subset does not establish equality on different target universes.

cards.title: Publish a defensible negative conclusion.
cards.decision: Retain the locked assessment where the incumbent did not demonstrate an advantage over a training-only mean.
cards.boundary: The consumed assessment is not reopened as a fresh selection set.

cards.title: Turn an exported result into a replayable artifact.
cards.decision: Regenerate the synthetic environment, recompute the output with the actual public engine, and reject stale source or altered evidence.
cards.boundary: The receipt verifies local computational consistency, not historical private-model performance.
